lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The floor keeps dropping out from under Toronto. A 4-0 loss to New Jersey on Sunday extended the Maple Leafs' skid to three games, and the damage went beyond the score: Colton Sissons left with a lower-body injury, while Morgan Rielly, Chris Tanev and Jack Roslovic were already unavailable. Connor Hellebuyck stopped 23 shots, but Toronto's larger problem was the familiar one - too little push when the game demanded it. At 8-9, the Leafs sit 10th in the Eastern Conference with 18 points, nine games behind, and the recent 2-4 loss to Montreal makes this more than a bad night; it is a wobble becoming a pattern. John Tavares' return offers some experience, not instant rescue. Tuesday's 7 p.m. ET meeting with Colorado is the test: can a battered lineup finally stop the bleeding?

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The offseason needed a jolt, and Aaron Parker supplied one with a bat instead of a press conference. Toronto's prospect went from last-minute substitute to Arizona Fall League Home Run Derby champion on Nov. 8, launching 19 homers and announcing himself as a name worth tracking after the Blue Jays finished 79-83, second in the AL East. The championship matters less as a forecast than as a reminder: this organization needs more dangerous bats, and Parker's power gives the development staff a live wire to shape - especially as he continues his transition from catcher to the outfield. Toronto's defense has earned trust; the offense and pitching now demand the hard decisions. Minor-league deals and option-year flexibility are useful housekeeping, not transformation. Watch whether the Blue Jays turn this early spark into an impact bat and reliable rotation help before spring training.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors have stopped the bleeding, but the bandage is thin. Toronto's 121-107 victory over Milwaukee on Nov. 6 restored a winning pulse and lifted the club to 5-4, good for third in the Atlantic Division - but this remains a team one injury away from being tested to the marrow. Scottie Barnes, who missed the Bucks game with left-adductor soreness, and Immanuel Quickley, nursing a right hamstring problem, practiced Sunday but remain questionable for tonight. Kawhi Leonard is still out with left-knee swelling, though he has rejoined the team for treatment. That is too much firepower sitting in street clothes for comfort. The Raptors have won two of their last three, but the schedule is about to demand proof, not promise. Tonight's 7:30 p.m. meeting with Memphis is the next examination: Toronto must show that the Milwaukee win was a foundation, not a reprieve.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: Washington's season is becoming a catalogue of missed chances, and Sunday supplied the latest exhibit: a 20-13 loss to the Rams, sealed by a baffling final drive that never truly threatened the end zone. At 2-5-1, Washington sits third in the NFC East, three games behind, with a one-game losing streak and precious little offensive rhythm. Jayden Daniels opened brightly, including a 42-yard completion to Van Jefferson, but the attack produced only three second-half points and finished with a lateral that went nowhere. The injury list made the task steeper - Terry McLaurin, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Jaylin Lane were unavailable, while center Lucas Patrick left with a concussion - but Dan Quinn was right: execution, not excuses, is the issue. Thursday night at the Giants is a must-win chance to stop the slide and prove this offense can finish.

article.title: Maple Leafs Lose 4-0 to Devils
paragraphs: The Maple Leafs were shut out 4-0 by the Devils on Sunday, with injuries continuing to pile up. Anthony Stolarz stopped 25 shots for Toronto, now 8-9 and 10th in the Eastern Conference. The Leafs host Colorado on Tuesday at 7:00 PM ET on TSN.

The Jays are looking ahead in the early offseason, with attention on how their prospects performed in the Arizona Fall League Fall Stars Game. The Raptors host the Grizzlies tonight at 7:30 PM ET. Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley are questionable, while Bittle and Leonard are out. Toronto enters at 5-4, third in the Atlantic Division.
